Feed.title: Philippine Cancer Society Delegation Prominent at UICC World Cancer Leaders’ Summit in Melbourne, Championing the New Global Declaration
Feed.content: The Philippine Cancer Society joined the UICC World Cancer Leaders' Summit in Melbourne, Australia, on 18–20 November 2025, together with other Filipino cancer groups. The delegation took part in talks on non-communicable diseases and in a workshop on ending cervical cancer through HPV vaccination and screening. The summit launched the World Cancer Declaration 2025–2035, which sets global goals for 2035, such as fewer cancer deaths and more cancers found early.

Feed.title: DOST-ASTI Convenes National Stakeholders to Build the FIRST Philippine Cervical Image Bank and Advance AI-Driven Screening
Feed.content: On 17 November 2025, DOST-ASTI hosted "AI Against Cervical Cancer," a hybrid meeting of research, government and civil society groups. They discussed building the first Philippine Cervical Image Bank for the Cerv.ai project, which makes AI tools to find early cervical cancer, and lower-cost HPV-DNA testing. The Philippine Cancer Society offered its mobile bus for screening in poor and far communities.

Feed.title: NCCN Partners with Philippine Cancer Organizations to Develop Locally Adapted Cancer Treatment Guidelines
Feed.content: The National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) is working with Philippine medical groups, including PSMO and the Society of Gynecological Oncologists of the Philippines, to adapt its cancer treatment guidelines to conditions in the Philippines. The planned guidelines cover 10 cancers: B-cell lymphomas, breast, colon, hepatocellular carcinoma (liver), lung, prostate, rectal, cervical, ovarian and uterine cancer. The aim is more consistent, evidence-based treatment for Filipino patients.

Feed.title: PANAG-ISTORYA: Conversations that matter in Cancer Care.
Feed.content: PSMO announced its 24th Midyear Convention, set for 16–17 April 2026 at the Dusit Thani D2 Hotel in Davao City. The theme, Panag-istorya (a Visayan word for dialogue), is about how cancer doctors talk with patients and families during hard moments, with a communication skills workshop led by Dr. Antonio Sison, who trained in psycho-oncology.

Feed.title: A Unified Front in Systemic Care: PSMO Reinforces the National Cancer Alliance
Feed.content: On World Cancer Day, 4 February 2026, PSMO joined the Philippine Cancer Society, the Philippine Society of Oncologists and the Philippine Medical Association at the PMA Auditorium. The groups signed a National Alliance memorandum of understanding on working together to make patient care pathways smoother, and launched a partnership between Quezon City and the City Cancer Challenge (C/Can).

Feed.title: BARANGAYAN GOES TO GINGOOG CITY!
Feed.content: On 16 August 2025, PSMO held a cancer awareness caravan for health workers at the Arturo S. Lugod Gymnasium in Gingoog City. Doctors, barangay health workers and cancer survivors talked about cancer basics, prevention, screening, treatment and common myths. It was done with the Department of Health, the Gingoog City government and the Philippine College of Physicians–Caraga Chapter.

Feed.title: Ano ang Sarcoma?
Feed.content: A short PSMO explainer in Filipino about sarcoma, a rare cancer that grows in bones and soft tissues such as muscle, fat, blood vessels, nerves, tendons and cartilage. It reminds readers that not every lump is cancer, but a swelling that lasts more than 2 weeks should be checked by a doctor.

Feed.title: Philippine Society of Medical Oncologists: A Vital Presence at the 1st National Patient Navigation Conference
Feed.content: PSMO took part in the 1st National Patient Navigation Conference on 26–27 June 2025 at Casa Ibarra, Pasay City. It was organized by the DOH Cancer Control Division, Amang Rodriguez Memorial Medical Center and the Philippine Cancer Society, and ended a training program that trained 61 patient navigators, who guide patients through cancer care.
